messages.subject: Temporarily suspend slider updates
parts:
I'm creating a page with two-way binding, where 15 sliders are updated when a new record is clicked.  There's one slider for each variable.  When the sliders are manually adjusted, the prediction models spits out a new result, and three graphs are redrawn.

Things are pretty slow when a new record is clicked, because three graphs are redrawn 15 times.  I'd like to avoid using Shiny's actionButton when sliders are manually adjusted by a human, because I love of silky responsiveness when only one slider is adjusted at a time.  Shiny's reactivity model is so smooth in this case, and users adjust sliders (which is quick) much more frequently than switch records.

Is there a way to suspend the sliders while I'm adjusting the whole batch?  If so, I think that would solve the performance concern, because 3 graphs would be redrawn, instead of 45 (=3*15) graphs.  I've used something similar C#'s SuspendLayout() and ResumeLayout() functions.  

If there's not a way to suspend/resume, am I missing a different approach (perhaps with isolate) in Lesson 8 that could help (that doesn't use the actionButton)?  Thanks, Will

UpdateSliders <- function() {
    ds <- Predicted() #Retrieves the subset of the larger data.frame that concerns the newly selected record.
    if( nrow(ds) < 1 ) return()

    a1 <- max(ds$A1) #This `max()` example is a simplification of the real version.
    a2 <- max(ds$A2)
    a3 <- max(ds$A3)
    ...
    a15 <- max(ds$A15)

    # Ideally the GUI updates would be suspended here.
    updateSliderInput(session, inputId="A1", value=a1)
    updateSliderInput(session, inputId="A2", value=a2)
    updateSliderInput(session, inputId="A3", value=a3)
    ...
    updateSliderInput(session, inputId="A15", value=a15)
    # Ideally the GUI updates would be resumed here.
}
